title: Where Does the Barcode Go on a Book Cover? KDP & IngramSpark Rules | SparkPrep
h1: Barcode placement on a book cover: KDP and IngramSpark rules
description: Where to put the ISBN barcode on your back cover, how much space to leave for KDP and IngramSpark, and how to fix a cover rejected for the barcode area or an ISBN mismatch.
lead: The barcode area is easy to get wrong: art or text sitting where the barcode goes, or a barcode that doesn't match the book's ISBN.
error: Text or images found in the barcode area / ISBN on cover does not match
errorNote: Paraphrased. Each printer words this differently.
why:
Printers and stores scan the barcode on the back cover, so it needs a clean, empty spot. KDP puts its own barcode in a 2" wide x 1.2" tall area in the lower right of the back cover if you don't add one. IngramSpark asks you to leave an area 1.75" wide x 1" tall free of text and graphics for it.

If your blurb, author photo or art runs into that area, the barcode can't be read and the cover is rejected. And if you use your own barcode, its ISBN has to match the ISBN you entered for the book, or it's rejected for an ISBN mismatch.

steps: On the back cover, keep the lower right corner clear: 2" x 1.2" for KDP, at least 1.75" x 1" for IngramSpark.
Keep a plain, light background behind the barcode so it scans.

diy.app: If you add your own barcode
steps: Make sure the ISBN under the barcode matches the ISBN in your book's setup, digit for digit.
Use a new ISBN for each format: paperback, hardcover and ebook each need their own.
IngramSpark's cover template already shows where the barcode goes. Design around it and delete the template guide layer before exporting.

cta.text: Not sure your back cover is clear? SparkPrep checks the barcode area and reads the ISBN on your cover against your book's ISBN, and flags any mismatch in minutes.

faq.q: Does KDP add the barcode for me?
faq.a: Yes. If you don't include one, KDP places a barcode in a 2 inch by 1.2 inch area in the lower right of the back cover, so leave that space empty.

faq.q: Can I use the same ISBN for paperback and hardcover?
faq.a: No. Each print format needs its own ISBN, and the barcode on each cover must match that format's ISBN.
